summary: Private (VPC): SSO/SAML login failures after customer IdP change (invalid signature / cannot validate assertion)
description:
RESTRICTED (Private customer). Do not paste customer screenshots with user identifiers into Slack. Keep customer domains, IdP entity IDs, and SAML assertion contents limited to this ticket.

Issue summary:
- Customer reports all SSO logins failing for Redwood Private Console after an IdP change (Okta -> new Okta app / cert rotation). Local break-glass admin works intermittently; most users blocked.

Customer impact:
- Console access blocked for all SSO users (admin + operators). Inference traffic continues but customer cannot view usage/latency dashboards or manage API keys/roles.
- Customer requested immediate mitigation and clear comms cadence.

Start time (customer reported):
- 2026-02-18 ~14:40Z

Environment:
- Redwood Private (VPC) control plane
- Region: us-west-2 (customer VPC)
- Auth mode: SAML SSO (IdP-initiated + SP-initiated enabled)

Symptoms / errors:
- Console login redirects back to /sso/callback then shows: "Authentication failed".
- In auth service logs: "SAMLResponse signature validation failed" and occasional "Audience restriction mismatch".

What changed:
- Customer rotated IdP signing certificate and updated the Okta SAML app. They also changed the EntityID/Issuer formatting (per their note).

Initial triage checklist (Support):
- Confirmed outage is limited to SSO; API inference calls continue.
- Requested: timestamp of failed attempts, user email (redacted), IdP metadata XML, expected ACS URL, EntityID/Issuer, whether they changed NameID format/attributes.
- Verified break-glass local admin still works (customer confirmed).

Escalation:
- Escalate to Private Deployments + Security/Auth SME due to Private SSO outage.
- Paging: Private Deployments oncall + Security escalation owner.

Customer comms plan (agreed):
- First update within 30 minutes, then updates every 60 minutes until mitigation; customer requested next update even if no new findings.

Requested customer-provided artifacts (restricted):
- IdP metadata XML (new)
- SAML assertion sample (if possible) or Okta event ID
- Screenshot of Okta app settings (redact usernames)
- Confirmation of the configured Redwood ACS URL and Audience URI they used
comments:
2026-02-18 15:02Z (Priya Shah - Support) - Ticket created from customer hotline. Marking as P1/Sev1: Private customer cannot access Console via SSO after IdP change. Inference traffic unaffected but operational access blocked.

2026-02-18 15:07Z (Owen Phillips - Support Eng, Assignee) - Acknowledged. Requested IdP metadata XML + confirm if cert rotated and whether Issuer/Audience changed. Asked customer to try break-glass local admin and confirm if at least one admin can log in.

2026-02-18 15:10Z (Rachel Kim - Enterprise CS) - Customer is asking for comms cadence + ETA. I set expectation: hourly updates; working with engineering now.

2026-02-18 15:33Z (Marcus Lin - Security Eng) - Looking. Two common causes after app recreation: (1) our SP config still has old IdP signing cert (signature validation fails), (2) Audience/Recipient/ACS mismatch if Okta app template changed. Need to verify what’s configured in Private auth service.

2026-02-18 15:40Z (Vivek Kulkarni - Private Deployments) - Can access customer’s private control plane config repo. Will check current SAML IdP metadata stored for their tenant and whether the new cert is loaded. Also checking if auth service caches metadata and needs restart.

2026-02-18 15:52Z (Owen Phillips - Support Eng) - Customer update #1 sent (hourly cadence): We have engaged Security + Private Deployments; investigating certificate + Issuer/Audience mismatch. Next update by 16:50Z.

2026-02-18 16:08Z (Vivek Kulkarni - Private Deployments) - Found tenant SAML config still references old IdP cert fingerprint. Their new metadata includes a different signing cert. Also saw recent change to "sp_entity_id" value in their config that does not match what Okta expects.

2026-02-18 16:12Z (Marcus Lin - Security Eng) - That explains signature validation failures. Plan: update stored IdP metadata to new XML, validate that our expected Audience (SP Entity ID) matches customer’s Okta Audience URI, then restart auth to flush cached metadata.

2026-02-18 16:20Z (Owen Phillips - Support Eng) - Asked customer to confirm what they set in Okta:
- Audience URI (SP Entity ID)
- Single sign on URL (ACS)
- Default RelayState (if any)
Also recommended temporary mitigation: use break-glass local admin for critical operations while we apply metadata update.

2026-02-18 16:31Z (Customer via Support) - Confirmed Okta settings:
- Single sign on URL: https://<redacted>/sso/callback
- Audience URI: https://<redacted>/saml/metadata
They changed Audience URI to match a doc they found internally.

2026-02-18 16:38Z (Marcus Lin - Security Eng) - Audience looks wrong: they set it to our metadata URL, not the SP Entity ID we expect. For Redwood Private we expect Audience == configured SP Entity ID (typically "redwood-private-console" or customer-specific URN), not the metadata endpoint.

2026-02-18 16:44Z (Vivek Kulkarni - Private Deployments) - Confirmed: current tenant expects SP Entity ID = "urn:redwood:private:<tenant-id>:console". Their IdP is sending Audience="https://<redacted>/saml/metadata" which triggers audience restriction mismatch. We should (a) correct their Okta Audience, and (b) update cert metadata on our side.

2026-02-18 16:50Z (Owen Phillips - Support Eng) - Customer update #2 sent: Root cause identified as mismatch between new IdP app settings and our expected SAML configuration (Audience + certificate). Provided exact Audience URI value to set (shared in restricted channel/email) and asked them to update. We are also updating our stored IdP metadata and restarting auth service to pick up the new signing cert. Next update by 17:50Z.

2026-02-18 17:05Z (Vivek Kulkarni - Private Deployments) - Applied change: updated IdP metadata XML for tenant to new signing cert. Restarted auth service in private control plane to clear cached metadata. Monitoring auth logs.

2026-02-18 17:18Z (Customer via Support) - Updated Okta Audience URI per instructions. Still seeing failures for some users; one admin login succeeded.

2026-02-18 17:26Z (Marcus Lin - Security Eng) - Partial success suggests Audience fixed but NameID/attribute mapping may differ between the old and new Okta app. Check for "user not found" vs signature errors.

2026-02-18 17:31Z (Owen Phillips - Support Eng) - Checked logs (provided by Private team): signature validation errors are gone. Now seeing "no matching user for NameID" for impacted users. Their Okta app is sending NameID in a different format (email vs persistent). We need them to send email or configure attribute "email".

2026-02-18 17:44Z (Owen Phillips - Support Eng) - Customer update #3 sent: Certificate/signature issue resolved; remaining failures due to NameID/attribute mapping changes in new IdP app. Requested they set NameID format to email and/or map "email" attribute. Next update by 18:50Z.

2026-02-18 18:03Z (Customer via Support) - Updated NameID to EmailAddress and mapped attribute "email". Users can now log in. Confirmed recovery.

2026-02-18 18:10Z (Vivek Kulkarni - Private Deployments) - Confirmed steady-state: auth logs clean; SSO success rate back to baseline. No further action required.

2026-02-18 18:22Z (Owen Phillips - Support Eng) - Mitigation complete. Asked customer to validate 2-3 additional users and both IdP-initiated + SP-initiated flows.

2026-02-18 18:40Z (Customer via Support) - Validated multiple users. SP-initiated and IdP-initiated both working.

2026-02-19 09:15Z (Owen Phillips - Support Eng) - Closing notes:
- Root cause: customer recreated/changed Okta SAML app which rotated signing cert and changed Issuer/Audience + NameID mapping; our stored IdP cert was outdated and their IdP configuration did not match our expected Audience + NameID.
- Fix: updated IdP metadata in Redwood Private tenant; restarted auth to pick up new cert; guided customer to correct Audience URI and NameID/attribute mapping.

2026-02-19 09:20Z (Priya Shah - Support) - Follow-ups:

3) Recommend adding a preflight validator in Private Console (surface actionable errors: signature invalid vs audience mismatch vs user mapping).
